subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What security boundary should OpenClaw use for inbound media isolation in multi-agent and multi-account deployments?
rationale: The source-confirmed gap spans core media storage, plugin channel ingestion, managed media references, sandbox staging, and upgrade behavior; choosing the scope key and compatibility model is a product/security decision, not a mechanical fix.

options.title: Design scoped media contract first
options.body: Adopt a single account/agent/channel/session-aware media contract with explicit sharing and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Accept narrow account scoping
options.body: Scope saves by channel account ID now, accepting that it may not cover multi-agent, multi-tenant, managed URI, and explicit-sharing cases without follow-up work.

options.title: Document current trust boundary
options.body: Keep flat inbound storage as an operator-managed trust boundary and document that multi-agent isolation requires separate instances or filesystem roots.

recommendation.title: Design scoped media contract first
recommendation.body: Adopt a single account/agent/channel/session-aware media contract with explicit sharing and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across managed inbound references and the existing issue review, making them the best available owner for the security-boundary decision.
